Ada Mensah
FIRMWARE / MOSSLINK

1 / CODE → PHYSICAL CHECK

How do you check a decision made in code?

Ada Mensah works with embedded firmware: code that controls a physical device. For Mosslink, an environmental sensor, she wrote the firmware, scheduled power states and built the bring-up fixture.

Bring-up means checking a new board’s basic operation. Follow the illustrative apparatus from a code decision to a bench observation. This is an explanatory model, not the actual device.

2 / ORGANIZE THE CYCLE

Give each activity its place.

Sleep → Measure → Transmit → repeat. Scheduling organizes different activities over a cycle, making the order of device behavior something you can inspect. Ada scheduled Mosslink’s power states.

The loop on the board is a teaching sequence, not recovered Mosslink firmware or measured timing. No durations or current values are represented.

3 / MAKE IT OBSERVABLE

A command needs a physical answer.

A firmware command asks the board to act. The bring-up fixture provides access to that board so its response can be observed on the bench. The fixture enables the check; the board’s circuitry makes the device work.

Ada: firmware, scheduling and fixture. A colleague: the PCB (printed circuit board) and analogue front end, the circuitry handling sensor signals. The connectors show relationships, not actual wiring.

4 / READ THE EVIDENCE

Two claims. Two kinds of support.

Measured sleep and transmit current, plus an assumed reporting interval, support a two-year endurance projection. A separate continuous bench run supports 72 hours observed. That run does not validate two years of endurance.

Neither path establishes field conditions or customer deployment. The instrument displays explain the claims; no original measurements table, trace, spreadsheet or run notebook is supplied.

5 / THE ANSWER & ITS LIMITS

Code, connected to a bench check.

Ada’s firmware and scheduling define device behavior; her fixture makes a physical board response accessible to observation. That is the connection from a code decision to a check on the bench.

Six of forty assembled engineering samples were bench-tested; none went to customers. One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished. The projection and bench run remain distinct evidence, with distinct limits.
